text:
mia: Heads up — since ~10:12 UTC we're seeing a big IOPS dip on ephemeral NVMe in eu-west3. GPU allocs are failing (attach timeouts) and provisioning backlog increased, triggering SLA alerts.

sam: on it. any correlation with janitor/scrub jobs?

mia: scrub backlog jumped at 10:09 and scrub throughput spiked across many nodes. quick metric: `sum by (host) (rate(nvme_write_iops[1m]))` shows a cluster-wide bump.

ops-bot: alert: gpu-provisioning-queue-length > 50 (eu-west3) — triggered at 10:14 UTC

liam: @nisha can you take oncall? this looks like a scrub <-> gpu scaling interaction.

nisha: oncall here. what's the immediate mitigation plan?

sam: short term we can throttle janitor/scrub work on the ephemeral pool for eu-west3. two options: patch the cronjob or use `scrubctl` to set a lower IOPS cap: `scrubctl set-rate --region eu-west3 --rate 0.3` (30% of normal). I'll apply the safer throttle first.

mia: logs also show KV-cache flushes stalling and attach RPCs hitting 20s timeouts, which makes the autoscaler think capacity is tight. SMART shows no disk errors. tail latency for small writes is >15ms on affected hosts.

nisha: any WAL / filesystem errors?

mia: none reported. it's capacity/queuing (iops/queue-depth) rather than hardware errors.

liam: root cause hypothesis: hysteresis gap in GPU autoscaler + sudden scrub ramp. We scaled up GPUs when pods queued, scrub concurrently ramped, then backoff oscillation made attach failures worse. We should add a cooldown/hysteresis to scale decisions.

sam: throttle applied at 10:20 UTC. scrub iops fell to ~30k per host within ~90s. probing GPU attaches now.

eva: requeued pending attach jobs — 32/38 succeeded so far, 6 still failing on the same 3 hosts. continuing retries.

nisha: good. immediate next steps: 1) keep scrub throttle for 1 hour, 2) add temporary 2m cooldown to autoscaler for eu-west3, 3) collect full perf traces and NVMe iops/latency windows during scale events.

sam: will open an ops PR with the throttle + autoscaler cooldown and include `grafana` panel links and the `nvme_io_stats` snapshot. PR target: today.

mia: can we also add a quick staging test to simulate scrub + massive scaleup to tune hysteresis? automated run would help avoid flapping.

nisha: yes — add a perf test in staging and file a follow-up to the scheduler: "make scrub scheduler backoff-aware of provisioning windows". I'll create the incident ticket and link this thread.

liam: long-term action: scheduler should detect high provisioning demand and either pause heavy scrubs or move them to lower-priority window. Also consider per-host scrub rate limits that respect attach latency SLOs.

nisha: agreed. thanks everyone for quick response. keep this thread updated if any hosts still fail after retries. :thumbsup:
